claim_one_line: THE LINE CENSUS (P-250; computed, no data): in B1656's frame at the canonical end two charged sectors coincide on a flat hypercharge line of order N exactly when N divides 4 or 5 (d = e), 6 (u = d), or 2 or 7 (u = e) -- their twist pairs agree up to swap and negation -- so every order from 8 on splits all three; a first generation is protected (R1 = 0) iff N divides its q_L - q_R or 3 (the Higgs's charge), so the only all-splitting protected order is 9 (the leptons) and no line protects the up quarks while splitting all three. Every line a principle on record selects (closure, move-invariance, the potential's half-period state, W63's tie, the tick's order-5 lines) leaves two sectors degenerate; W59's order-9 lines are an input. Corrections: P-170's 'down never' fails at order 3; the delta-rule (W88: d = e iff N | 8 or 10) is not B1656's -- orders 8 and 10 split d from e at every L up to 1e8, so the seat's frame question is answered: not the end. The first census's printed prediction failed twice; the corrected laws held on fresh data at a new tau and at omega. 0 of 19.
